identity.title: Cloud-scale Molecular Gas Properties in 15 Nearby Galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: PHANGS-ALMA is mapping the CO (2-1) emission from a large sample of nearby star-forming galaxies ($74$ in total)

question.value: How do cloud-scale (45-120 pc) molecular gas velocity dispersion, surface density, virial parameter and turbulent pressure vary within and among 15 nearby galaxies?

evidence.quote: We measure the velocity dispersion, $\sigma$, and surface density, $\Sigma$, of the molecular gas in nearby galaxies from CO spectral line cubes with spatial resolution $45$-$120$ pc

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Channel width 2.5 km/s (5.0 km/s for M51 and Antennae; 2.6 for M33)

evidence.quote: The channel width for most of these observations is $2.5$-$2.6$ km s$^{-1}$.

arrays.value: ALMA 12-m, 7-m and total power for PHANGS targets

evidence.quote: These targets were observed by ALMA in CO (2-1) using the 12-meter and 7-meter interferometric arrays as well as the total-power antennas.

angular_resolution.value: Native 0.6-1.7 arcsec (34-130 pc); convolved to 45-120 pc

sensitivity.value: 1 sigma channel rms 0.06-0.27 K at native resolution; ~0.5 K km/s integrated for PHANGS

evidence.quote: the sensitivity of velocity-integrated intensity maps are typically ${\sim}0.5$ K km s$^{-1}$

observing_dates.value: First 11 PHANGS targets observed in 2016, ALMA Cycle 3

evidence.quote: the first $11$ targets analyzed here were already observed in 2016 during ALMA’s Cycle 3
we include the PdBI Arcsecond Whirlpool Survey (PAWS) CO (1-0) map of M51
we use the CARMA CO (1-0) survey by A. Schruba et al. (in prep.)
For M33, we use the IRAM 30-m CO (2-1) survey by (cite: Gratier_etal_2010) and (cite: Druard_etal_2014).
we include the ALMA CO (3-2) map of the interacting region of the Antennae galaxies presented by (cite: Whitmore_etal_2014)
Distance values are taken from the Extragalactic Distance Database (cite: Tully_etal_2009).
*all other galaxies* - S$^4$G global stellar masses (cite: Sheth_etal_2010; Querejeta_etal_2015).

what.value: Milky Way cloud catalog used for beam-dilution test

evidence.quote: we take the molecular cloud catalog published by (cite: MivilleDeschenes_etal_2017) as a reference sample

masking.value: Seed: >=2 consecutive channels S/N>=5; expand to adjacent pixels with >=2 channels S/N>=2; extend in velocity to +-3 sigma Gaussian equivalent

evidence.quote: we first identify all 3D regions in the data cube where $\geq 2$ consecutive channels show emission with signal-to-noise ratio ${\rm (S/N)} \geq 5$.

array_combination.value: PHANGS cubes include 12m, 7m and total power; Antennae lacks short spacing

evidence.quote: This is the only target in our sample that lacks short- and zero-spacing data.

smoothing.value: Convolved to round Gaussian beams of 45, 60, 80, 100, 120 pc FWHM; resampled to Nyquist-sampled grids

evidence.quote: we pre-process all data sets by convolving them to a set of round Gaussian-shaped beams with fixed linear sizes: $45$, $60$, $80$, $100$, and $120$ pc (at FWHM).

what.value: PHANGS-ALMA observing strategy and data reduction described elsewhere

evidence.quote: A detailed description of the PHANGS-ALMA sample, observing strategy and data reduction is presented in A. K. Leroy et al. (2018, in prep.).

analysis_steps.goal: Convolve cubes to fixed linear resolutions

method.value: Convolve to round Gaussian beams and resample to Nyquist grids

evidence.quote: we resample the data sets onto regular square grids so that the pixels Nyquist-sample the new beam
When the native angular resolution of a data set is coarser than the target beam size, we exclude that galaxy from the analysis at that spatial scale

analysis_steps.goal: Identify significant CO sightlines and measure I_CO, T_peak

method.value: Two-stage S/N mask (5 sigma seed, 2 sigma expansion), velocity growth to +-3 sigma; compute integrated and peak intensity per sightline

evidence.quote: we calculate the line-integrated intensity $\mbox{$I_\mathrm{CO}$}$ and peak intensity $\mbox{$T_\mathrm{peak}$}$ of the emission within the expanded mask.

validation.value: 1,000 Monte Carlo noise realizations with fixed mask give statistical errors

evidence.quote: We generate $1,000$ realizations of the data cube by artificially adding random noise to the original cube

method.value: Sigma = alpha_CO * I_CO with fixed conversion factors

evidence.quote: We adopt the following conversion factors $\mbox{$\alpha_\mathrm{CO}$}\equiv \mbox{$\Sigma$}/\mbox{$I_\mathrm{CO}$}$

assumptions.value: Galactic alpha_CO; CO(2-1)/(1-0)=0.7, CO(3-2)/(1-0)=0.25; no inclination or filling-factor correction

evidence.quote: we do not apply any correction to $\Sigma$ to account for beam filling factors or the effect of galaxy disk inclination.

method.value: Effective width sigma = I_CO/(sqrt(2pi) T_peak), corrected in quadrature for spectral response

evidence.quote: we subtract the effective width of the spectral response from the measured effective width

key_parameters.value: sigma_response from channel width and channel-to-channel correlation r, measured from empty channels

evidence.loc: Quantifying the Spectral Response Curve Width of the CO Maps
evidence.quote: we measure $r$ from the correlation between noise in successive empty spectral channels in the data cube
we do not correct for unresolved rotational motions or contributions from multiple clouds along the line of sight.

validation.value: r at 60 pc compared with Leroy et al. 2016 k values

evidence.loc: Quantifying the Spectral Response Curve Width of the CO Maps
evidence.quote: which are consistent with those reported by (cite: Leroy_etal_2016) (see Table 3 therein).

analysis_steps.goal: Derive virial parameter and turbulent pressure

method.value: alpha_vir = 5 sigma^2 r_beam/(fGM) with R=r_beam; P_turb ~ Sigma sigma^2/(2R)

evidence.quote: we take the beam size as the relevant size scale (i.e. $R = \mbox{$r_\mathrm{beam}$}$, thus $R = 40$ pc at $80$ pc resolution), adopt $f=10/9$

assumptions.value: Line-of-sight depth ~2 r_beam; density profile rho ~ r^-1 (f=10/9)

evidence.quote: In this paper, we take $l \sim 2\mbox{$r_\mathrm{beam}$}$

method.value: log sigma = beta log(Sigma/100) + A with intrinsic scatter, truncated likelihood, only sightlines above 5-sigma criterion

evidence.quote: We include only the data points above our 2-consecutive-5-sigma selection criterion

fitting.value: emcee affine-invariant ensemble MCMC, uninformative priors, Gaussian likelihood with statistical covariance in both axes and intrinsic scatter, truncation normalization

evidence.quote: We adopt a Bayesian approach with an uninformative prior, and find the best fit model parameters, as well as their estimated uncertainties, by sampling the posterior distribution

validation.value: Mock distributions recover input parameters; other fitting methods differ by ~0.05

evidence.quote: We find that the input parameters can be accurately recovered as long as the truncation does not severely affect the whole distribution.

method.value: Add noise to M33 cube to match NGC 2835 noise and repeat analysis

evidence.quote: We add random noise into the M33 data cube to artificially degrade it, so that its noise level matches that in the data cube for NGC 2835

validation.value: Compared with beam-diluted Milky Way cloud catalog

evidence.quote: we calculate their “beam-averaged” surface density as $\mbox{$\Sigma$}' = \mbox{$\Sigma$}\;R^2 / r_{\rm beam}^2$
Our implementation is based on the Python package `emcee` (cite: Foreman-Mackey_etal_2013)

results_numeric.quantity: Intrinsic scatter in sigma at fixed Sigma

evidence.quote: We find the intrinsic scatter in $\sigma$ at fixed $\Sigma$ to be less than $0.10$ dex for all galaxies at all resolutions.
Most galaxies (excluding M31 and M33) have distributions centered near $\mbox{$\alpha_\mathrm{vir}$}\approx 1.5$-$3.0$

results_numeric.quantity: Median alpha_vir M31 / M33 at 120 pc

evidence.quote: this sample corresponds to nearly $30,000$ independent beams across our sample

results_numeric.quantity: M33 recovered mass fraction after noise degradation

evidence.quote: the recovered molecular gas mass faction in M33 drastically drops from 63% to 8%

results_numeric.quantity: Center vs disk median Sigma offset in strongly barred galaxies

evidence.quote: the median $\Sigma$ value in the central region can be $0.8$-$1.7$ dex higher than in the disk.

results_numeric.value: varies by >4 orders of magnitude (disk 10^3-10^5 low mass, 10^5-10^7 high mass K cm^-3)

evidence.quote: The mass weighted median $P_\mathrm{turb}$ varies by more than $4$ orders of magnitude across our sample.

findings_qualitative.value: The sigma-Sigma relation is approximately constant-alpha_vir across disks, while P_turb varies enormously with environment

evidence.quote: This indicates only weak variation in the virial parameter $\alpha_\mathrm{vir}\propto\sigma^2/\Sigma$

findings_qualitative.value: Central regions of strongly barred galaxies show elevated sigma at given Sigma

evidence.quote: The same quantities appear enhanced in the central kpc of strongly barred galaxies relative to their disks.

claims.hypothesis: Molecular gas at cloud scales has a common dynamical state across galaxies
claims.experiment: Fixed-scale sigma and Sigma measurements and power-law fits for 15 galaxies
claims.result: slope 0.34-0.63 per galaxy, combined 0.47; median alpha_vir 1.5-3.0
claims.finding: Gas is near energy equipartition with weak alpha_vir variation

evidence.quote: suggesting a common dynamical state for molecular gas in most of our targets at $45$-$120$ pc spatial scales

claims.hypothesis: Turbulent pressure varies strongly with environment
claims.result: Median P_turb varies by >4 dex; centers up to 2-3 dex higher
claims.finding: Internal pressure depends strongly on environment and galaxy mass

evidence.quote: The internal pressure of a patch of molecular gas is clearly a strong function of environment.

claims.hypothesis: The sigma-Sigma relation flattens at low Sigma
claims.experiment: M31/M33 high-sensitivity maps; degrade M33 noise; beam-diluted MW clouds
claims.result: M31/M33 show high sigma at low Sigma; degraded M33 follows alpha_vir~2
claims.finding: Flattening is genuine in low-density environments, from beam dilution, missing gas and external pressure

evidence.quote: This leads us to expect the flattening at low $\Sigma$ to be a genuine feature in low molecular gas density environments.

claims.hypothesis: The sigma-Sigma correlation is not an artifact of the effective-width definition

evidence.quote: This result confirms that our observed line width-intensity relation is not artificial in nature

why_this_method.value: Fixed-scale approach avoids segmentation criteria that find beam-sized objects and is simple to apply to simulations

evidence.quote: Based on all these, we believe that the fixed-scale approach is at least as appropriate in this context as cloud identification.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Cloud-identification (Clumpfind, cprops) rejected in favor of fixed-scale approach

evidence.quote: Our fixed-scale approach differs from the cloud identification approaches commonly used in previous studies

limitations_admitted.value: Single alpha_CO adopted; absolute alpha_vir uncertain; beam smearing not corrected in centers

evidence.quote: We adopt a single $\alpha_{\rm CO}$ and then discuss possible variations when they become relevant.

referee_caveats_inferred: Beam size taken as cloud size; alpha_vir absolute values depend on assumed geometry
Heterogeneous data sets (different lines, line ratios, sensitivities, missing short spacings in Antennae)
Selection effects at low Sigma bias medians in NGC 2835 and NGC 5068
Sigma and effective width correlated by construction (partly addressed)
